title: there was/were there has/have been there will be
subtitle: there was / there has been / there will be
summary: Use there was/there were for the past, there has/have been for the present perfect, and there will be for the future.

lesson.heading: there was / there were
lesson.text: At the station a woman looks at the train times. **There is** a train every hour. The time now is 11.15, so the 11 o'clock train has gone: **there was** a train at 11 o'clock. We use **there was** and **there were** to talk about the past.

examples.text: The time now is 11.15. **There was** a train at 11 o'clock.
**There was** a good film on TV last night.
We stayed at a very big hotel. **There were** 550 rooms.

left.label: there is / there are (present)
examples: **There is** a good film on TV tonight.
We are staying at a very big hotel. **There are** 550 rooms.
**Are there** any phone messages for me this morning?
I'm hungry, but **there isn't** anything to eat.

right.label: there was / there were (past)
examples: **There was** a good film on TV last night.
We stayed at a very big hotel. **There were** 550 rooms.
**Were there** any phone messages for me yesterday?
I was hungry when I got home, but **there wasn't** anything to eat.

lesson.heading: there has been / there have been
lesson.text: Two cars have crashed in the street. A man sees it and says to his friend: 'Look! **There's been** an accident.' **There's been** = there **has** been. We use **there has been** and **there have been** for the present perfect.

examples.text: This road is very dangerous. **There have been** many accidents.
Last week I went back to my town. **There have been** a lot of changes.

lesson.heading: there was with a finished time
lesson.text: When we say *when* something happened (last night, last Friday, ten years ago), we use **there was**, not there has been.

examples.wrong: There has been an accident last night

examples.text: **There was** a party at the club last Friday.

lesson.heading: there will be
lesson.text: A man on television points at a weather map and says: '**There will be** rain tomorrow afternoon.' We use **there will be** for the future. The negative is **there won't be** (= there will not be).

examples.text: Do you think **there will be** a lot of people at the party on Saturday?
The manager is leaving, so **there will be** a new manager soon.
I'll do my packing today because **there won't be** time tomorrow.

lesson.heading: All the forms
rows: there has been / there have been
there hasn't been / there haven't been

lesson.text: Use **there was** with one thing and **there were** with more than one: *there was a carpet*, *there were three pictures*.

exercises.prompt: Last week the room was not empty. ___ a carpet on the floor.
exercises.explanation: A carpet is one thing, so we say there was.

exercises.prompt: ___ three pictures on the wall near the door.
exercises.explanation: Three pictures is more than one thing, so we say there were.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginning of each sentence with its ending.

pairs.left: There was a good film on TV
We stayed at a very big hotel. There were
I was hungry, but there wasn't
The manager is leaving, so there will be
This road is dangerous. There have been

exercises.prompt: *A:* Did you buy any eggs? *B:* No, ___ any in the shop.
exercises.explanation: any eggs = more than one, so we say there weren't.

exercises.prompt: *A:* ___ many people at the meeting? *B:* No, very few.
exercises.explanation: In past questions was/were comes first: Were there many people ... ?

exercises.prompt: Is the sentence about the past or about the future?

items.text: There was a party at the club last Friday.
There will be a new manager soon.
Ten years ago there were 500 children at the school.
Were there any phone messages for me yesterday?
Will there be a lot of people at the party?

exercises.explanation: 24 hours is more than one, and it is true now, so: There are.

exercises.prompt: When you arrive tomorrow, ___ somebody at the station to meet you.
exercises.explanation: tomorrow = future, so we use there will be.

exercises.prompt: Last week I went back to the town where I was born. It's very different now. ___ a lot of changes.
exercises.explanation: a lot of changes = more than one, so: There have been.
With a finished past time (last night) we use there was.

exercises.statement: There has been an accident last night.
exercises.explanation: There was an accident last night. We use there was when we say when it happened.

exercises.prompt: You want to know about Saturday's party. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: Do you think there will be a lot of people at the party?
exercises.explanation: After think the order is there will be, not will there be.
